title: Echo Benchmarking Harness for CI-driven Performance Regression Detection
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce an 'Echo Benchmark' CI job that performs a compact, deterministic performance comparison between the current baseline and a PR change. The harness will run a small, representative subset of production traffic patterns (token-length distribution, request inter-arrival) in an isolated sandbox and measure throughput (tokens/sec), p95 latency, and tail behavior. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by code changes before merge, with lower CI cost and faster feedback than full baseline runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- CI job runs on PRs touching runtime or scheduler code.
- Job completes within 10 minutes and consumes <= 2 GPU-seconds (by synthetic limits).
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec, p95 latency, p99 latency, error rate reported to PR checks.
- Regression detection uses a Bayesian posterior comparison that flags ~1% false positive target.
- PRs with statistically significant degradation are blocked and include reproduction artifacts (mini-profile, flamegraph link).
technical_notes: Design: use small deterministic synthetic model (Echo model) that returns token-for-token responses to eliminate model variance. Replay sampled production traces with sequence-length buckets. Use ephemeral CI runner with local CUDA/GPU or CPU-fallback quantized path. Persist baseline snapshots (hash -> metrics) in a lightweight artifact store (S3 prefix) keyed by main branch commit. Regression logic: compute posterior distribution of throughput ratio; flag if probability > 0.975 that PR is worse by > 5%.
implementation_steps: 1) Build echo-synth binary container that can accept a workload spec and emit token-level timestamps. 2) Implement workload sampler service to produce fixed seeds for sequence lengths and inter-arrival timing. 3) Add CircleCI/GitHub Actions workflow step 'echo-bench' to runtime repo with permissive routing for PRs. 4) Implement lightweight artifact store and baseline registerer (upload on main branch CI). 5) Implement Bayesian comparator script and PR annotation integration. 6) Wire results into PR checks and console link to per-run dashboard.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: synthetic workload may not catch regressions that only appear under full production mixing. Mitigation: keep workload updated from production sampling and add stratified buckets for long-tail payloads.
- Risk: CI cost growth. Mitigation: enforce time and GPU budget and only run on relevant file globs; fall back to cheap CPU-path for non-GPU changes.
- Risk: false positives blocking merges. Mitigation: tuned posterior threshold, allow 'flaky' label to bypass, and provide quick rollback run button.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Khan: Initial proposal drafted. Focus on low-cost CI feedback loop rather than exhaustive coverage.
2025-02-24 - Diego Martinez: Spike executed using local container. Measured baseline tokens/sec stable across 10 runs with stddev < 2%.
2025-02-27 - Lina Park (SRE): Suggested adding a p99 and tail-sampling bucket to capture long-tail regressions. Also recommended enforcing a strict GPU time budget on CI runners.
2025-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Implemented Bayesian comparator prototype. Using a 5% effect-size threshold and 0.975 posterior cutoff yields ~0.8% false-positive in historical replay.
2025-03-03 - Product: Requested PR annotation format to include quick link to repro artifacts and a 'rerun bench' button in the PR UI.
